concerns.text: Phase 6.5 (T044–T050) implements 'Cross-Cultural Stylometric Validation' and introduces new regression predictors (voice_alignment_score) that are entirely absent from spec.md (US-1 to US-4) and plan.md. This constitutes unapproved scope creep and violates the constraint that tasks must not silently relax or expand the spec's defined scope without explicit authorization.

Task T010 hardcodes 45 Project Gutenberg IDs and references an OSF URL with empty parentheses '()', failing to define the source of the human annotations required by SC-001 (50 stories). This creates an untestable dependency on non-existent external data, violating the requirement that every acceptance criterion must survive into a task's verification step.

Task T030 requires aligning external reader-response data by computing SHA-256 hashes of 'full_text' and matching against a local Gutenberg corpus. This contradicts the spec's assumption (Assumptions section) that external datasets contain 'textual descriptions of scenarios' rather than full narrative texts. The requirement to match exact text hashes makes the task impossible to execute against standard external moral-judgement datasets, violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax what the spec demands (i.e., the feasibility of the data linkage).

The 'Revision Note' states 'Phase 7 (Cross-Cultural Stylometric Validation) has been removed to align strictly with spec.md,' yet the Phase 6.5 section containing tasks T044–T050 remains fully present and unchecked. This internal contradiction leaves orphan tasks in the execution list, violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax or contradict the plan's stated scope.

Task T025 runs matching 'using the primary threshold (a predetermined value)' but does not specify where that value is defined or how it relates to the sensitivity analysis sweep range {0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40} mandated by FR-006. This risks a disconnect between the validation run and the sensitivity analysis, violating the requirement that every acceptance criterion (FR-006) must survive into a task's verification step.
